partner_result_applied.scope_used: C0 output for rank>=3 with a nonzero original-coordinate diagonal entry; isolates diag(A)=0 as the complementary rough-input regularity class

other_dependencies.scope: continuous density and matrix-dependent height for any invertible physical 3x3/4x4 affine product quadratic, plus principal-block reduction
exact L-infinity extremal transfer to measure-one product indicators and bounded finite-fragment sets
sharp universal constant equals smooth compact-input and C0-output envelopes

new_result.statement: For every independent cap-one product input and every real symmetric A with rank(A)>=3, X^TAX has a bounded density in C0(R). For a chosen invertible principal block B of order d=3 or4 the available height is C_d/sigma_min(B), hence instance-dependent.
new_result.new_local_tail: For an invertible d=3 or4 block, the pushforward restricted to |x|>=R has interval-density constant <= d^(3/2)/(sigma_min(B) R). After completing the square, p(t)<=d^(3/2)*sqrt(2||B||)/(sigma_min(B)*sqrt(|t-c0|)).
new_result.target_reformulation: The sharp universal constant equals the supremum of attained pointwise maxima over finite-fragment measure-one product-indicator witnesses; if infinite, there is a genuine sequence of continuous attained peaks tending to infinity.

first_unproved_step: Prove one dimension- and matrix-independent bound on sup_t p_Q(t), equivalently on the attained maxima of the finite-fragment extreme outputs, or construct a target-valid sequence whose maxima diverge.
next_step: Combine the current ridge-certified low-leverage spectral window with a source-valid high-leverage/product-bank aggregate mechanism; do not pay a single deteriorating principal minor or use a refuted cross-rank dichotomy.
